content.text: surgery is delayed until HTN is controlled w alpha- + beta-blockers, usually phenoxybenzamine 20 to 40 mg PO 3 times a day; BP target < 130/80; blockade is presumed effective after ~10 to 14 days (CV re-equilibration); intraop hypertensive paroxysms: phentolamine 1 to 5 mg IV or nitroprusside infusion.

Initially 10 mg twice a day. Increase every other day, usually to 20 to 40 mg 2 or 3 times a day, until optimal (BP control). Start small and ↑ slowly until the desired effect or side effects from blockade become troublesome.

CI: conditions where a fall in BP may be undesirable; hypersensitivity to the drug or any of its components. Alpha blockade leaves beta receptors unopposed; compounds that stimulate both receptor types may produce an exaggerated hypotensive response and tachycardia. May interact w/ epinephrine to produce an exaggerated hypotensive response and tachycardia. Case reports of carcinoma in humans after long-term tx; long-term use not recommended. Use w/ caution in marked cerebral or coronary arteriosclerosis or renal damage; blocking effect may aggravate symptoms of respiratory infections. Adverse reactions: postural hypotension, tachycardia, inhibition of ejaculation, nasal congestion, miosis. OD Sx: postural hypotension w/ dizziness or fainting, tachycardia (esp postural), vomiting, lethargy, shock. OD tx: discontinue the drug; treatment of circulatory failure is a prime consideration. Epinephrine is contraindicated in OD (net effect is vasodilation and a further drop in BP: epinephrine reversal). IV levarterenol bitartrate may be used for severe hypotensive reactions (stimulates alpha-receptors primarily).
